provenance.method: Representation Router planning-review principles applied to the four World Builder page views already built; records the choice, not a tool-generated score or visual certification. No sketch set was put to Brian for these views; the chat thread follows his words of 2026-11-17.

question: Can a person describe a world in one conversation and run it, find earlier worlds and runs, branch from a round beside the original, and be told before running when a world would stall?

views.question: How do I describe a world and refine it?
views.rationale: Describing and refining is a conversation: one message box under a thread of messages, with the AI's questions as suggestion chips and the current draft as a card; Run builds the latest draft. Brian, 2026-11-17: "the ui should just be more like chatgpt with a run button so that its not really a fully separate dialogue box".
alternatives: A separate dialogue box beside a description box (the previous design; rejected by Brian 2026-11-17).

views.question: Which worlds and runs do I have?
views.rationale: A name-ordered list with each world's runs and branches nested under it, searchable and pinnable; a list answers 'which one' better than a graph.
alternatives: A graph of worlds and runs (kept for a single world's run ancestry only if the list proves too deep).

views.question: How did this branch differ from the original?
views.rationale: Comparing two runs of one world from the same round is a spatial comparison: the two room maps side by side at the same round, with one slider.
alternatives: A diff table of events (answers what, not where).

views.question: Will this world run, or stall?
views.rationale: A single plain-words notice above the run status, shown before any round is paid for; a chart would add nothing.
alternatives: Silent run that ends after a quiet round (the previous behaviour).
